newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Peter Guilford briefed on the results of a survey of EU business active in China, pointing to key remaining obstacles to trade and investment. He said main obstacles were a lack of transparency of the legal system, corrupt practices, import quotas and restrictions to market.

Guilford said Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan would meet Chinese State Council Secretary General Zou Zheng Ping and Hong Kong and Macao State Council Bureau Director Lu Ping in the afternoon. He said he would be available to brief reporters afterwards.
Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said she hoped the French Channel blocade would be lifted today.

Lambert said the Commission had sent a letter to French Transport Minister Bernard Pons on Wednesday underlining the French commitment to compensate hawlers who have suffered financially from France's road haulage dispute in November.

In answer to a question on the Italian reaction to the Commission spring economic forecasts released on Wednesday, spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission had recognized Italy's progresses in the reduction of its public deficit since one or two years. Van der Pas also reminded that the Commission had recognized in a footnote that if the measures taken had full effectiveness and if additional measures were taken, Italy's 1998 deficit to GDP could come down to the 3.0% required by the EU Treaty to acceed to the EMU.

Asked about the doubts Commissioner Emma Bonino expressed on the economic forecast figures, van der Pas said the Commissioner had not qualified the figures to be wrong but different to figures she had seen previously.

Van der Pas said Commission President Jacques Santer had said the figures were no political decision but an authoristation to release technical figures and would therefore not politically bind the Commissioners.
Van der Pas said Commissioner Mario Monti was happy with this footnote a solution for the Italian issue.

Spokesman Filippo di Robilant said the Commission found it odd that the fishing sector reacted to the net size regulation 18 months after it was taken. He also said the Commission was available to review the decision on the request of a Member State.

Spokesman Patrick Child said the Commission economic forecasts were based on an unchanged economic policy whereas some national concergence programmes measures had not yet been implemented in concrete measures and could therefore not be taken into account by the Commission services.
Van der Pas said Commission President Santer and himself were members of Commissioner Bonino's fan club.
The Commission released the following documents:

- IP/97/343: ECU 13 million for urban renewal in Rotterdam and Utrecht in the Netherlands.
- IP/97/344: Commission aid for Kiel.
- IP/97/345: Commission approves the acquisition of joint control of J.M. Voith GmbH by Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank.
- IP/97/346: EU business points obstacles in trade and investment in China.
- IP/97/347: 174 sports projects win funds under EURATHLON.
- IP/97/348: Improving and simplifying the business environment for business start-ups.
- Speech/97/96: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson on " Innovative research and appropriate health care for the citizens of Europe".
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Research and development No 1997-1: R&D in the EU.
- European Cohesion Forum - Media Programme.
- ME97/24.4: Midday Express.
